title: Library service and fine strategies
idea: The core design is one LibraryService facade that runs borrow, return and reserve, with the clock, fine rule and notifier passed in as interfaces.

analogy.text: A circulation desk clerk follows the rule binder on the desk. Swap the fines page in the binder and the clerk works the same way.
analogy.breaks: A clerk can bend a rule; the service never does.

points: Facade: callers use LibraryService and never touch copies or queues directly.
Strategy: FinePolicy decides the fine, so new fine rules are new classes.
Observer-style Notifier tells a waiting member their copy is ready.
An injected Today clock makes due dates and fines testable and repeatable.

hero.title: Borrow, reserve, then a late return

steps.caption: M-1 borrows ISBN-1. The service finds free copy CP-1 and opens loan LN-1.
M-2 asks for the same title. No copy is free, so the service refuses.
M-2 reserves instead. The service appends M-2 to the ISBN-1 queue.
Three days late, M-1 returns CP-1. The service closes LN-1.
The queue is not empty, so CP-1 goes on the hold shelf for M-2.
The `Notifier` tells M-2 the copy is ready at the desk.
The `FinePolicy` prices the late days, and the fine goes back to the caller.

code.title: Service and interfaces
code.caption: The core flow. Clock, fine rule and notifier are interfaces given to the constructor. The next pages add loan states and thread safety. The unpaid-fine block from the scope page is a second check beside the loan limit; it is left out to keep the file short.

walk.text: Wire the service with a hand-moved clock, a per-day fine and a printing notifier.
One copy: M-1 gets it, M-2 is refused and reserves instead.
Move the clock, return late, then M-3 and M-2 both ask for the copy.
Three interfaces: today's date, the fine rule and the message channel.
Borrow checks the loan limit, then takes a free copy or one held for this member.
Return closes the loan, hands the copy to the queue head, and prices the fine.
A test clock you move by hand: real code passes a system clock.

code.title: A new fine rule
code.caption: Open/closed in practice: a new FinePolicy that skips closed days. The service and the old rule are not edited.

walk.text: A copy due on a Monday comes back eight days later.
Two policies side by side: the plain one and the new one.
Count only late days that were open days, then apply the same rate and cap.

pitfalls: Do not call LocalDate.now() inside the service; inject a clock instead.
Do not branch on fine type with if-else; add a FinePolicy class.
Do not let callers edit a copy's status; route every change through the service.

quiz.q: What does CoreLibrary print when M-3 asks for ISBN-1?
quiz.why: CP-1 is on the hold shelf with `heldFor` set to M-2. The filter matches it only for M-2, so M-3 finds nothing.

takeaway: One facade runs the rules; every policy that may change is an interface.

starters: Why is the reservation queue per ISBN and not per copy?
When would I split LibraryService into smaller services?
How do I test FinePolicy without the rest of the service?
